chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“If the pilgrim visits from Minā, then leaves Makkah, passes beyond the houses of Makkah, sleeps, and then reaches morning before coming to Minā, then there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.بُيُوتَ: the houses or dwellings marking the inhabited area of Makkah
key_terms.فَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no obligation, penalty, or liability upon him
key_terms.فَنَامَ: he slept, indicating the passing of the night
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred city from which the pilgrim departs here
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the sacred location connected to the rites of hajj

ai.seo_question: When is there no penalty upon a pilgrim who spends the night away from Minā during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling related to the pilgrim’s movement between Minā and Makkah during hajj. It states that if the pilgrim leaves Makkah, passes beyond its houses, sleeps, and then morning comes before he returns to Minā, no liability or penalty is due upon him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3012 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"If a pilgrim visits from Mina, leaves Mecca, passes by the houses of Mecca, sleeps, and then wakes up before returning to Mina, there is no obligation upon him."
